segments.t: korTTY's visual configuration spans three tabs: KTPH001AppearanceKTPH002 controls the app-level UI design, KTPH003FontKTPH004 configures terminal typeface and size, and KTPH005ThemesKTPH006 manages reusable terminal color profiles. All settings persist to KTPH000.
Customize the application window and dialog visual style.

AtlantaFX Primer Dark, AtlantaFX Primer Light, AtlantaFX Nord Dark, AtlantaFX Nord Light, AtlantaFX Cupertino Dark, AtlantaFX Cupertino Light, AtlantaFX Dracula, Default, Matrix Terminal, Holographic Interface, Klingon Tactical, Elegant Dark, Amber CRT, Synthwave '84, Gruvbox Retro, Nord Arctic, Dracula
Automatic (theme), Original, Paper, Midnight, Cyberpunk, Retrowave, Forest, Ocean, Terminal, GPT, Cute

The KTPH000 and KTPH001 buttons next to the dropdown step backward and forward through the designs (wrapping around at the ends). When a design other than KTPH002DefaultKTPH003 is selected, a preview image of that design is shown below the controls; the KTPH004DefaultKTPH005 design has no preview and shows a short note in its place.
KTPH000Enable design animationsKTPH001 doubles as a reduce-motion switch: turning it off stops the animated design effects while leaving the colors in place.

The seven AtlantaFX entries apply AtlantaFX 2.1.0's KTPH000Primer DarkKTPH001, KTPH002Primer LightKTPH003, KTPH004Nord DarkKTPH005, KTPH006Nord LightKTPH007, KTPH008Cupertino DarkKTPH009, KTPH010Cupertino LightKTPH011, or KTPH012DraculaKTPH013 user-agent theme to native JavaFX controls, with a small korTTY overlay for the main window chrome and korTTY-specific controls. They are grouped at the top of the dropdown, and a new installation starts with KTPH014AtlantaFX Primer DarkKTPH015. Existing settings are not migrated: an existing KTPH016DefaultKTPH017 selection stays Default. Changing to Default or any older korTTY design restores JavaFX Modena before that design's stylesheet is applied. The change is live across open windows, dialogs, menus, tooltips, and completion popups.

KTPH000Chat color profileKTPH001 themes the AI chat and swarm surfaces. The default KTPH002Automatic (theme)KTPH003 derives its palette from the active terminal theme's agent-panel colors; the other profiles are fixed palettes.

App Design applies only to korTTY's application windows and dialogs. Terminal sessions, the Monaco file editor, session-journal pages, and AI chat content retain their own independent color settings (configured via the Colors or Themes tabs or their own appearance controls).

KTPH000UI font sizeKTPH001 scales korTTY's own interface — the menu bar and its dropdowns, dialogs, form labels, buttons, tab titles, the dashboard, the file browser and the status bar. It takes effect the moment you save; no restart is needed, and windows that are already open resize with it. The main window's first-launch size grows along with it, and dialogs and the manual window that remember their size are re-measured after a change rather than reopening at a size that no longer fits their text.
It deliberately does KTPH000notKTPH001 touch surfaces that already have their own size control, so the two never fight each other:
Where its size is set instead
The KTPH000FontKTPH001 tab, plus the View menu's zoom shortcuts
AI chat, agent plan and activity panels
The KTPH000 / KTPH001 buttons in its own window — see KTPH002belowKTPH003

Two further parts of the interface keep their size at every setting: the macOS application menu (the one in the system menu bar), because macOS draws it rather than korTTY, and the AI swarm status strip, whose labels are painted onto a canvas together with hand-computed positions.

KTPH000Match display resolutionKTPH001 derives the size from the primary display instead, and disables the number field while it is on. A new installation starts with it KTPH002onKTPH003, so korTTY fits itself to the screen before anyone visits this tab; updating an existing installation never changes it — whatever you had stays. The value comes from the display's KTPH004logicalKTPH005 height — the resolution the operating system reports after its own scaling:

This is why a Retina MacBook stays at 100 %: macOS already scales it, so it reports roughly 1100 logical pixels and needs no help. The case the option exists for is a 4K or 5K display running at 100 % operating-system scaling, where korTTY really does get the full 2160 or 2880 pixels to draw into.

Automatic is a suggestion, not a measurement. JavaFX cannot report a display's physical size, so korTTY cannot tell a 27-inch 4K panel from a 32-inch one at the same resolution, even though they need different sizes. If the result does not suit you, turn the option off and set the percentage yourself — your manual value is remembered while automatic is on.

Automatic tops out at 140 % and the manual setting at 160 %. The ceiling is deliberate: a handful of dialogs size themselves from fixed pixel widths, and beyond that point their text starts to crowd. korTTY re-reads the display when you save the settings, so after changing your monitor setup, open Settings and save again (or restart) to pick up the new resolution.

The manual (KTPH015Help → ManualKTPH016, KTPH017KTPH002KTPH018) has its own text size. Three buttons at the top left of its window control it: KTPH000, the current percentage, and KTPH001. The percentage is also the reset control. Click it to return to 100 %. There are keyboard shortcuts for all three: KTPH019KTPH003KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH004KTPH022, KTPH023KTPH005KTPH024+KTPH025KTPH006KTPH026, KTPH027KTPH007KTPH028+KTPH029KTPH008KTPH030. On Windows and Linux they are KTPH031KTPH009KTPH032+KTPH033KTPH010KTPH034, KTPH035KTPH011KTPH036+KTPH037KTPH012KTPH038, KTPH039KTPH013KTPH040+KTPH041KTPH014KTPH042. They are registered on the manual's own window, so they never collide with the terminal zoom in the main window.

The range is 70–250 % in steps of 10, wider than the interface setting because the manual is a reflowing document rather than a layout built from fixed widths. The size is remembered across restarts, applies to the AI search answers next to the manual as well, and stays put as you navigate between pages. It scales the page as a whole — text, images and diagrams together — the way a browser's zoom does.

This is separate from KTPH000UI font sizeKTPH001 above, which governs the buttons and window chrome KTPH002aroundKTPH003 the manual. If the manual's own toolbar looks too small, that is the setting to change.
Set the terminal and editor typeface and size.
Common monospace fonts (Monaco, Courier New, Menlo, Fira Code, etc.) and all system fonts

The Font tab sets global defaults for all new terminal connections. Individual connections can override these values via their own connection settings. A live preview is shown as you adjust the controls.

Create, edit, and manage terminal color themes. Themes define the text, background and cursor colors and the styling for all terminal sessions; the 16 ANSI colors and the selection color come from KTPH000ColorsKTPH001. The theme list sits on the left with its buttons underneath; the rest of the tab is a preview of a terminal screen in the selected theme (see KTPH002Theme previewKTPH003).
Create a new custom color theme

Open the selected theme in the theme editor, built-in themes included. The change is saved to KTPH000; an edited built-in theme keeps its KTPH001(built-in)KTPH002 label and still cannot be deleted. Duplicate it first if you want to keep the original
Copy the selected theme as a new custom theme
Remove a custom theme (built-in themes cannot be deleted)
When enabled, applying a theme also changes font family and size.
When this option is enabled, selecting a theme from the Colors tab's color profile dropdown will also apply that theme's font family and size. When disabled, only the theme's colors are applied.

korTTY includes a set of built-in color themes (e.g., Default, Dark Mode, Solarized Light). Built-in and custom themes are stored together in a single file, KTPH000. All themes appear in the Colors tab's color profile selector and in connection-specific theme dropdowns.
Built-in themes can be edited but not deleted, and korTTY does not restore their original colors on its own. To keep the original, duplicate the theme first and edit the custom copy.

A theme's KTPH000Terminal AI agent panelKTPH001 colors start out derived from its terminal colors: the panel keeps the terminal's background with a faint tint of an accent color, which is the theme's cursor color, or blue when the cursor is white or grey. The AI agent's KTPH002designsKTPH003 use them.

To the right of the list, a mock terminal screen shows what a session looks like in the selected theme: a prompt and an KTPH000 listing (directories, an executable, a symlink and an archive in their usual colors), a KTPH001, a compiler warning and error, a test summary, a row of all sixteen ANSI colors (normal, then bright) and a second prompt with the cursor in the theme's cursor color and shape (block, underline or bar). Background and text use the theme's colors; the font is the theme's own when KTPH002applying a theme also changes font family and sizeKTPH003 is on, otherwise the Font tab's. The sixteen ANSI colors are taken from the Colors tab as it is set right now, unsaved changes included, so you can judge a theme and a palette together before saving. Below the mock, three swatches show the AI agent panel's background, run and error colors, which do not appear in a terminal session. The preview updates when you select, add, edit or duplicate a theme.
KTPH000Colors tabKTPH001: Choose a theme via the "Color Profile" dropdown; if the Themes tab's font option is enabled, the selected theme's font is also applied.
KTPH000Connection settingsKTPH001: Each individual SSH connection can override the global font and theme via its own settings (accessible in Connection Manager or Quick Connect).
KTPH000Terminal emulationKTPH001: Font and theme colors affect only the terminal content; the application UI style (menu bar, dialogs, tabs) is determined by the Appearance tab's app design setting.
